image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) swimming in blue water. The duck features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a chestnut-brown breast, and a greyish body. It has a bright yellow bill and is captured mid-swim with visible ripples in the water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and bright yellow, matching the description for a mallard drake.
The eye is visible on the side of the head and appears dark/black, consistent with the species.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is typical of a swimming duck, appearing streamlined and buoyant. The plumage texture looks dense and waterproof.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, chestnut breast, and grey flanks.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange webbed foot is visible paddling underwater. The anatomy (webbing, color, position) is correct for a swimming duck.
The folded wing is visible on the side of the body, showing proper feather layering and structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, short and slightly upturned, consistent with the 'drake feather' characteristic.
